purpose: Resolve, or state the exact limitation for, every active Hotspawn CS2 fixture that the featured exact-name line could not price. HLTV first (identity and ranking), then esportsbook and exchange lines. No probability, pick or alias is written by this file; it records what the official sources published and what that means for the ladder.
method_order: 1. Hotspawn fixture identity and scheduled start (fixtures API + match page).
2. HLTV match page and team pages for identity, start time and published ranking.
3. Polymarket event and market records (Gamma API) for a two-sided prematch series price.
4. Only a two-sided book inside the published spread ceiling can produce a pick; an in-play price never can.

lines.title: Counter-Strike: Spirit Academy vs Sökerorg (BO3) - CCT Europe Series #12 Group Stage
lines.detail: Polymarket's official event record gives eventStartTime 2026-10-25T12:25:00Z and its Map 1 market was quoted 0.999 / 1.000 with a last trade of 0.999 when read, i.e. the map was already decided. The market is therefore in play and cannot produce a prematch pick.

fixtures.conclusion: No prematch pick is derivable for 1081156 at observation. Hotspawn schedules the fixture for 12:00Z while Polymarket's official record starts it at 12:25Z, a 25-minute disagreement that is outside the ladder's 60-second identity window (scripts/originate.py START_TOLERANCE_SEC = 60), and by 13:44Z the only market was in play. Neither an in-play quote nor a post-hoc rating is published as a prematch probability.
limitations: In-play prices are excluded by policy; they are not prematch picks.
The 25-minute Hotspawn/Polymarket start disagreement exceeds the 60-second join tolerance by design.
HLTV ranks both teams (#111 / #167) but publishes no points for either, so the HLTV rung cannot price them.
fixtures.recommendation: When Hotspawn and a provider disagree on start time, record the rejection in the fixture's research trail (the published trail for 1081156 showed only 'no unique exact-name fixture'), so a reader can see that a market existed and why it did not join. Any widening of the join window is a policy change and needs review.

lines.title: Counter-Strike: HOTU vs The Huns Esports (BO3) - Moscow Cyber Games Playoffs
lines.detail: The official Match Winner market exists at the same 09:00Z start and displayed 65¢ HOTU / 35¢ The Huns Esports (last trade 58¢), but its two-sided book is 0.38 / 0.92 — a 0.54 spread, far outside the 0.15 acceptance ceiling — with $690 volume. It is a real market with an unquotable book, not a missing market.

published_estimate.label: bo3.gg results network
published_estimate.detail: The board currently prices this fixture 98.2% HOTU from the uncalibrated results-network model, which diverges from the only money observation (0.65 implied for HOTU) by about 33 points. Read from the published origination card; the checked-in data/origination.json in this checkout predates the snapshot, so the replay against the live board is recorded here and re-checked by the publisher each refresh.

fixtures.conclusion: A market does exist and the identity join is correct (the registered alias 'The Huns Esports' -> 'The Huns' is scoped to Moscow Cyber Games 2026 and matches the same 09:00Z start). The book is 0.54 wide, so it cannot produce a compliant pick; the published 98.2% is a labelled research model, not a line. A third-party forecast does exist: HLTV displays HOTU 76.0% / The Huns 24.0% for this fixture (read 14:00Z). It is recorded here as evidence, not published as this project's probability, because the published-line policy admits observed two-way prices and Valve ratings only; adopting a third-party forecast rung is requested as review item 0962-R08.
limitations: The only two-sided book is 0.54 wide, above every published ceiling; policy rejects it as a line.
The published model estimate diverges from the market's implied price by about 33 points.
HLTV ranks both teams but publishes no points below rank 30, so the HLTV rung cannot price them.
fixtures.recommendation: Publish the market midpoint next to the model estimate as guidance-only context so a reader can see the disagreement, and keep the model label on the pick. Any change to rung precedence is a policy decision and needs review.

valve_rows.why_it_does_not_price: Two complete five-player Valve rows carry the name 'The Huns' (944 and 701 points), and HLTV's current lineup (Bart4k, controlez, Cozen, DarkMeister, bexyz) is an exact five-player match for neither, so the fail-closed uniqueness rule in scripts/domain.py:valve_analysis refuses to choose a roster.
